applies_why: Yes; the judge makes UNDERDETERMINED rest on the sign's sense being open after the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, which is the forbidden treatment of a two-sense or non-stating verse as open.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. — reading one: two senses leave the sign open and support UNDERDETERMINED; reading two: both senses stand and the sign is not open.
why: K-S2 says a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand, so using the sign's open sense as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED breaches the rule.
